main_text.p: certiùs, eodem ferè cum Epi[illegible, ~9 letters] ippenses & ad Philemonem tempore, exaratam. Ubi ipsissima illa restitutionis suæ, & [?]παρακλήσεως pollicitatio, Philip. 1,26. Philem. 22. prout, quæ Philippensium fuerat ergà Paulũ sollicitudo, constantiũ ἀναγκαίως τῇ αὐτῇ ἀλλήλων Phil. iv. 14. eadem fuerat & Hebræorum, probationiũ συμπαθείαν τοῖς αὐτοῖς ὁμοίοις[?], Hebr. x. 34. prout etiam, quem ad Philippenses ablegarat Timotheum, Phil. ii. 19, brevi reducem sibi fore pollicebatur, adeóque & comitem itineris ad Hebræos instituendi, Hebr. xiii. 23. Scripta ergò ad Hebræos Epistola, nonnihil post illam ad Philippenses, prioribus Pauli vinculis vel solutis, vel jam jam solvendis. Adeóque biennio illo, quo liberâ in custodiâ Romæ detentus, vel expleto, vel mox explendo. Ut de suo ad Philippenses, & Philemonem, & Hebræos adventu, certius jam quid pronunciare potuerit. Consentiunt Baronius, ad annum Christi LX. Blondellus, præfat. in Apolog. pro Hieron. Us-serius, Annalium parte ii. sub finem, & si

page.notes: Top-left page number and running head are partly obscured by blots; "208" and the middle words of the running head are uncertain. Greek words are only partly legible through the blots (the Greek in lines 2 to 4 is especially doubtful); the Greek letters given are best readings. "Epi[...]" on the first line is illegible because of a blot. Show-through and ink blots in the body were not transcribed. The catchword "qui" is printed below the last line at the right.
